From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: hosting preference & origin migration (ACME-3472)

Hi Jordan / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap + asks so we can align next steps: 

What we heard from your team:
- Primary concern: predictable latency and data residency for PII-sensitive features.
- Current environment: a mix of internal Triton endpoints and a legacy GPU cluster (you mentioned some on-prem nodes).
- Traffic shape: mostly low baseline with short spikes during product experiments (goal ~6–8 QPS peak for the initial rollout).

Decision points we need from Acme to recommend a final hosting path: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem. For each please confirm:
1) Which origin are you migrating from? (OpenAI API / other LLM API / self-hosted Triton / legacy GPU cluster)
2) Do you require a customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment for compliance?
3) Any hard latency SLOs (p95 / p99 target) and token budget constraints?

Recommended quick path (proposal):
- Phase 1: Private deployment (VPC) with a short Dedicated reservation for steady throughput — allows us to meet residency + low-latency needs and validate KV caching.
- Phase 2: Lift-and-shift of low-risk endpoints, then cutover heavier traffic after smoke tests and quality checks.

I attached two stubs: Redwood Dedicated pricing (pdf) and a short migration walkthrough with a proposed 6-week onboarding timeline.

Can you confirm the origin (answer to #1) and whether Procurement should be looped now? If you prefer Hosted API we can also provide an isolation + encryption profile but would need to scope RBAC and KMS requirements.

Thanks — I’m happy to jump on another 30-min session with Karthik and Marissa to map capacity and the runbook.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0179

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-ACME-3472.pdf (pricing sheet, 3 pages); acme-migration-walkthrough.pdf (onboarding checklist, 6 pages)

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-ai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme-ai.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme-ai.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 13:43:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: hosting preference & origin migration (ACME-3472)

Thanks Priya — good summary. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Which origin are you migrating from?
We are migrating from a self-hosted stack: internal Triton endpoints fronting a legacy GPU cluster (on-prem; 8x A100 style nodes). We also have some experimental traffic hitting OpenEndpoint wrappers but the production traffic is on-prem.

> 2) Do you require a customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment for compliance?
Yes — we need a Private VPC with customer KMS. On-prem preferred for the most sensitive buckets, but a VPC-first approach that guarantees data never leaves the region is acceptable.

> 3) Any hard latency SLOs (p95 / p99 target) and token budget constraints?
Target: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 400ms for our 256-token median flows. Token budget: aiming to keep monthly usage under equivalent of $12k in hosted spend initially.

If Private VPC is the recommended path, what does the onboarding look like for migrating the Triton models and preserving KV cache behavior? We are worried about cold-starts and tokenization parity.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of ML Platforms | Acme AI
j.ellis@acme-ai.com

Karthik / Marissa — Jordan confirmed they are coming from an on-prem Triton / legacy GPU cluster and require Private VPC + customer KMS. Please see the high-level plan I proposed to the customer below and advise on capacity + migration ownership: 

Proposed onboarding slices (6-week target):
- Week 0: Access + networking setup (VPC peering, KMS exchange, audit access).
- Week 1–2: Proof-of-concept on subset of models (run in Redwood Private with Dedicated reservation of baseline capacity). Validate latency & token parity.
- Week 3–4: Lift-and-shift remaining endpoints, enable KV prefix caching + continuous batching, run load tests targeting p95/p99.
- Week 5–6: Quality ramp, rollback plan, SLA acceptance and cutover.

Karthik: can you provide an initial Dedicated sizing estimate to cover 8x A100-ish baseline with 2x headroom for spikes? Also list required autoscaling/burst config so we can map to cost.
Marissa: can you draft a migration runbook template (model artifacts, tokenizer checks, KV cache migration steps, smoke tests) and share by Wed?

Jordan — we can start with a 4-week POC if you prefer; the POC cost can be covered by a short-term dedicated commit. If Procurement wants numbers, Karthik will include monthly commit options in his note.

Thanks — looping in operations so the networking and security folks have a single source of truth.

Best,
Priya
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
